seo.title: Best Working Cafes in Almaty (2026) | tabiji.ai
seo.metaDescription: Discover the top 12 cafes in Almaty perfect for remote work. Enjoy fast Wi-Fi, great coffee, and comfortable settings, from cozy spots to vibrant hubs.

hero.subtitle: Almaty's burgeoning remote work scene thrives in a vibrant cafe culture, offering a mix of stylish, quiet, and buzzing spots perfect for productivity and inspiration.

picks.name: Nedelka
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Nedelka is a long-standing favorite, beloved for its spacious interior, ample natural light, and a consistent buzz that fuels creativity without being overly distracting. They offer excellent Wi-Fi, comfortable seating perfect for long sessions, and a delicious menu of breakfast, lunch, and baked goods. It's an ideal spot to spend a full workday.
picks.whatToOrder: Their signature Syrniki (cottage cheese pancakes) with a Flat White. Don't forget to grab a fresh croissant.
picks.insiderTip: Arrive before 10 AM on weekdays to secure a prime spot near a window or power outlet, as it gets busy quickly. They have multiple levels, so explore for quieter corners.
picks.redditQuote: "Nedelka is my go-to in Almaty. Reliable Wi-Fi, great coffee, and their Syrniki are just next level. I swear half the city works from there."

picks.name: Bowler Coffee Roasters
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Known for its exceptional quality coffee and minimalist, industrial-chic aesthetic, Bowler Coffee Roasters is a serious contender for focused work. They roast their own beans, ensuring a fresh and potent brew. While smaller than some, it offers a quieter atmosphere conducive to deep work, especially during off-peak hours, with strong Wi-Fi.
picks.whatToOrder: A V60 Pour Over with their seasonal single-origin bean, paired with a fresh Croissant.
picks.insiderTip: If you need an outlet, look for spots along the walls or near the shared tables. They also sell beans if you want to take the excellent coffee experience home.
picks.redditQuote: "Bowler's is where I go when I really need to concentrate. The coffee is unmatched, and the vibe is chill enough to get serious work done without interruptions."

picks.name: Urban Coffee
picks.whyItMadeTheList: With multiple locations across Almaty, Urban Coffee is a reliable choice for remote workers seeking a modern and comfortable environment. Their Dostyk Avenue branch is particularly spacious, offering plenty of seating options, decent Wi-Fi, and a diverse menu that goes beyond just coffee to include substantial sandwiches and salads, perfect for a working lunch.
picks.whatToOrder: A large Cappuccino and their Chicken Avocado Sandwich.
picks.insiderTip: Their window seats offer great people-watching opportunities and ample natural light, perfect for daytime working. Some locations can get louder, so check the atmosphere upon arrival.
picks.redditQuote: "You can always count on Urban Coffee for solid Wi-Fi and a comfy chair. It's not fancy, but it gets the job done when you need to grind for a few hours."

picks.name: Travelers Coffee
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Travelers Coffee is a well-established chain with a cozy, rustic-chic ambiance that makes it feel like a home away from home. The Zhibek Zholy location is particularly vibrant, offering a great spot to work with reliable Wi-Fi, comfortable armchairs, and a menu featuring a wide range of coffee drinks, teas, and delicious desserts to keep you energized.
picks.whatToOrder: Their rich Americano and a slice of their famous Carrot Cake.
picks.insiderTip: Head to the back sections or upstairs for potentially quieter spots with more privacy. They have good power outlet availability, especially near the banquettes.
picks.redditQuote: "Travelers Coffee is a classic for a reason. Good Wi-Fi, comfy seats, and I can actually get work done without feeling rushed. Plus, that Carrot Cake!"

picks.name: Kaffeesatz
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Kaffeesatz offers a unique German-inspired cafe experience with a focus on quality coffee and authentic pastries. It's generally a quieter spot compared to some of the larger chains, making it excellent for focused work. The cozy, warm interior and friendly staff create a welcoming environment for digital nomads seeking a peaceful retreat.
picks.whatToOrder: A strong Espresso and their traditional German Apple Strudel or a Brezel.
picks.insiderTip: They have limited seating, so try to visit during non-peak lunch hours for the best chance of getting a table with access to power. Their breakfast menu is a great way to start a productive day.
picks.redditQuote: "Kaffeesatz is my secret weapon for quiet work days. The coffee is robust, the strudel is amazing, and I never have trouble with their Wi-Fi."

picks.name: JumpinGoat Coffee & Tea
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Bringing a touch of Australian coffee culture to Almaty, JumpinGoat is known for its high-quality coffee, vibrant atmosphere, and excellent brunch options. The cafe has a modern, airy feel with plenty of natural light, making it a pleasant place to work. While it can get lively, the strong Wi-Fi and good food options make it a solid choice for a few hours of productivity.
picks.whatToOrder: A classic Flat White and their Avocado Toast with poached eggs.
picks.insiderTip: Grab a table near the back for a slightly calmer environment, away from the main entrance traffic. They have some outdoor seating which is lovely in warmer months if you don't mind potential noise.
picks.redditQuote: "JumpinGoat's Flat White is the best in Almaty, hands down. I can usually snag a spot and get some emails done, even with the lively vibe."

picks.name: Teplitsa (Теплица)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Teplitsa, meaning 'Greenhouse', truly lives up to its name with a lush, plant-filled interior that offers a refreshing escape from the city bustle. While a bit further from the absolute city center, its unique, serene ambiance makes it a fantastic spot for creative work or longer, focused sessions. Expect good Wi-Fi, comfortable seating, and a wholesome menu.
picks.whatToOrder: Their Green Smoothie and a bowl of their healthy Buddha Bowl, accompanied by an Americano.
picks.insiderTip: This place is perfect for a full-day work session if you're looking for tranquility. Call ahead to reserve a spot if you plan to visit during peak lunch hours, especially on weekends, as it's very popular.
picks.redditQuote: "Teplitsa is my absolute favorite. Working surrounded by plants just feels good, and their food is so fresh. Wi-Fi is strong too!"

picks.name: Buno Coffee
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Buno Coffee is a charming independent cafe focusing on high-quality coffee and a warm, inviting atmosphere. It's a smaller, cozier spot perfect for individual work or quiet meetings. The friendly baristas, consistent Wi-Fi, and delicious pastries make it a local gem for those seeking a less corporate feel for their remote work needs.
picks.whatToOrder: A meticulously prepared Cappuccino and their rich Chocolate Lava Cake.
picks.insiderTip: The cafe can fill up quickly, especially in the mornings. Look for the window bar seating for a comfortable individual workspace with a view.
picks.redditQuote: "Buno's is my quiet little spot. The Wi-Fi always works, the coffee is great, and it's small enough that it rarely gets too loud to concentrate."

picks.name: Big Apple Coffee Shop
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Big Apple Coffee Shop offers a classic American diner-style experience with a modern twist, making it a great spot for a productive breakfast or lunch work session. It's known for its hearty portions, diverse menu, and consistent service. The atmosphere is generally lively but well-managed, with reliable Wi-Fi to keep you connected.
picks.whatToOrder: Their famous Breakfast Burrito with a bottomless filter coffee.
picks.insiderTip: They open early, making it perfect for early risers who want to get a head start on their day before the crowds. Power outlets are available but might require a bit of searching during busy times.
picks.redditQuote: "Big Apple is where I go for a solid breakfast and to knock out some work. The portions are huge, the coffee keeps flowing, and their Wi-Fi never lets me down."

picks.name: Coffeeboom
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Coffeeboom is one of Almaty's most ubiquitous coffee chains, making it a highly accessible option for remote workers across the city. While it can be bustling, especially its larger branches, it offers reliable Wi-Fi, affordable pricing, and a vast menu of coffee drinks, snacks, and light meals. It's a practical choice for impromptu work sessions.
picks.whatToOrder: Their Caramel Macchiato and a piece of their Napoleon Cake.
picks.insiderTip: Seek out their smaller, less central locations for a potentially quieter experience. The one on Nazarbayev near Kabanbay Batyr is quite spacious. Don't expect a super quiet library atmosphere, but it's great for background noise.
picks.redditQuote: "Coffeeboom is basically everywhere, and the Wi-Fi is always decent. It's my emergency work spot when I need a quick fix and cheap coffee."

picks.name: Barista
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Barista is a stylish cafe chain that strikes a good balance between a comfortable working environment and a vibrant social space. The Shevchenko Street branch, with its modern decor and spacious layout, provides ample room for laptops. They offer good quality coffee, decent food, and generally reliable Wi-Fi, making it a solid choice for productive hours.
picks.whatToOrder: A classic Latte and their Smoked Salmon Bagel.
picks.insiderTip: Look for tables towards the back or in quieter corners if you need to take a call. Power outlets are available, but might be competitive during peak times.
picks.redditQuote: "I like Barista for its consistent vibe and good coffee. It’s a good middle-ground when I want to feel like I’m 'out' but still need to get work done. Wi-Fi's always good."

picks.name: Oasis Coffee
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Oasis Coffee is a charming independent cafe with a relaxed, bohemian vibe, popular among students and creative professionals. It's known for its commitment to high-quality coffee beans, delicious homemade desserts, and a selection of vegan-friendly options. The atmosphere is generally calm and conducive to focused work, with dependable Wi-Fi and comfortable seating.
picks.whatToOrder: Their unique Lavender Latte and a slice of homemade Vegan Cheesecake.
picks.insiderTip: The cafe has a cozy, somewhat eclectic interior. Head to the larger communal table or the window bar for the best working spots. It's a great place to discover local artists' work often displayed on the walls.
picks.redditQuote: "Oasis Coffee is such a hidden gem. Great coffee, super chill atmosphere, and I've never had an issue getting my work done there. Plus, their vegan cakes are divine!"

faq.question: What are the typical operating hours for working cafes in Almaty?
faq.answer: Most working cafes in Almaty generally open between 8:00 AM and 9:00 AM, and close around 10:00 PM to 11:00 PM. Some popular spots like Nedelka or Big Apple Coffee Shop might open earlier for breakfast, while smaller, independent cafes may have slightly shorter evening hours. Always check specific cafe hours online before you go.

faq.question: Do Almaty cafes usually have good Wi-Fi and power outlets for laptops?
faq.answer: Yes, the vast majority of cafes catering to the working crowd in Almaty offer free and reliable Wi-Fi, often with speeds sufficient for video calls and uploads. Power outlets are common, especially in cafes popular with students and remote workers, but they can be competitive during peak hours. It's always a good idea to arrive early if you absolutely need an outlet.

faq.question: Is it acceptable to work for several hours in an Almaty cafe?
faq.answer: Absolutely! It is very common and accepted to work for several hours in Almaty's cafes, especially in those known for attracting digital nomads and students. To be a considerate patron, make sure to order periodically – perhaps a coffee every hour or two, or a meal – to support the business for the space you're occupying.

faq.question: What's the average cost for a coffee and a light meal at a working cafe in Almaty?
faq.answer: On average, you can expect to pay between 2,500 KZT to 6,000 KZT ($6-14 USD) for a coffee and a light meal or pastry at a working cafe in Almaty. Specialty coffee shops might be on the higher end, while chains like Coffeeboom offer more budget-friendly options. Prices can vary depending on the specific items ordered.

faq.question: Are there any cafes in Almaty that are particularly quiet for focused work?
faq.answer: For particularly quiet and focused work, consider places like Bowler Coffee Roasters or Kaffeesatz, especially during off-peak times (mid-morning or late afternoon). Teplitsa, though further out, offers a uniquely serene environment. Larger chain cafes can be hit or miss depending on the location and time of day, often having more background buzz.

faq.question: Do Almaty cafes typically have English-speaking staff or English menus?
faq.answer: In most popular working cafes in Almaty, especially those frequented by tourists and expats, you'll find at least some staff who speak basic English. Many cafes also provide English menus or digital menus accessible via QR code. Don't hesitate to use translation apps if you encounter any language barriers, as Almaty is generally quite welcoming.

methodology: Our selection of Almaty's best working cafes is based on extensive local research, factoring in reliable Wi-Fi, ample power outlets, comfortable seating, coffee quality, noise levels, and the availability of snacks or meals. We've prioritized venues that cater specifically to the needs of digital nomads and remote workers, blending functionality with an authentic Almaty experience.
